To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) users' Web experience levels are related to the number of criteria that users consider when judging the credibility of a web page, and to the importance they give to each of these criteria, and (b) the criteria users take into account when judging the credibility are related to the importance they assign to each of these.

Users with more Web experience were found to have higher credibility judgments for Web pages, to be more skeptical of Web pages in general, to be more aware of Web credibility criteria, to be more likely to use Web credibility criteria when evaluating pages, and to be more likely and able to identify the source of a page."

1) Web experience levels have an effect on user credibility judgments; 2) the more experienced users are more likely to judge a website's credibility based on its content, and less on its appearance; and 3) Web experience levels do not have a significant impact on users' judgments of a website's usefulness, or the likelihood that the user would recommend the site to a friend.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: What is the impact of users' Web experience levels on the criteria they use to judge the quality of information they find on the Internet?
the question of how users evaluate the information quality on the Web and what factors are used to judge information.
the relationship between users’ Web experience and the criteria they use to judge the credibility of Web information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
users' experience levels have a significant effect on the importance they assign to different criteria.
users with a higher level of Web experience tend to use a more sophisticated set of criteria to judge the credibility of a website than users with a lower level of Web experience.
the more Web experience a user had, the less importance he or she attributed to the criteria "source" and "design" of Web pages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the higher the Web experience level of the users the more important the criteria of the information source and the content of the Web site are for the credibility judgments.
users with a higher Web experience level were more critical and used a broader range of criteria to judge the quality of their information sources.

the more experienced a user is, the more he/she relies on the quality of the content and the less he/she relies on other factors such as the source of the information, the design of the Web page or the reputation of the author.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Web experience level has an effect on how users judge the credibility of Web sites.
the Web experience level of the users is not the only factor affecting their credibility judgments.
users who have more experience with the Web are less likely to rely on the visual cues of the Web pages and are more likely to consider the content and author of the information.
